Welcome to the second day of the conference. Before the first session, a word about the coffee break. It is twenty-five minutes long, and it is not a pause: it is where most of our delegates find the people they work with later. If you have never been to one of our events, here is the advice we give everybody. Do not stand with the colleagues you came with. Ask a question about the talk you have just heard. And if the conversation stops, ask the other person what they have enjoyed most so far. It has worked for fifteen years.

Hi Thiago, this is Mark from the Chicago office. Nothing urgent, I just wanted to say it was good to meet you today. I have never worked with the Sao Paulo team before, so this was new for me. A few of us are going to watch the race on Sunday at my place, and there will be food and far too much noise. You said you have followed Formula 1 since you were a kid, so I thought of you. Let me know. See you tomorrow.

First, Thiago finds himself alone at the coffee table with a stranger. Then he uses an icebreaker about the talk they have just heard. After that, she brings up her first trip to South America. Next, they find common ground in Formula 1 and the conversation gets easier. Finally, they agree to catch up at the dinner and he goes back to the session.
